dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. Good afternoon, how can I help you?

Hi, yeah. Let me explain what's going on, because it's a bit of a sequence. There's a sidewalk near the school that never got cleared after the storm, and I'd like to know when somebody's going to get to it.
Okay, the sidewalk by the school. Which school are we talking about, do you know?

Sure. It's the elementary school over on the stretch by the little crosswalk. Sorry, hang on, I've got my work laptop open, I'm typing something while we talk. Okay. So the school, the sidewalk on the side facing the street, the one the kids walk along.
Alright. And you said this was after the storm. Is that the one from last weekend, Sunday into Monday?

Right, the snow-to-rain one. So Sunday it snowed, then Monday it turned over to rain and everything got heavy and slushy, and then it froze up. That was two days ago. The street was plowed, I'll give them that. But the sidewalk is still a solid packed sheet of it.
So the road got plowed but the sidewalk by the school wasn't touched at all. Is that right?

Not touched. Not shoveled, not blown, nothing. I walked it Monday afternoon, and again this morning. Same thing. People are walking out in the road to get around it. [pause] Sorry, one second, I'm just sending this line. Okay.
No problem. Do you have a cross street or a nearby landmark so I can put it on the report correctly?
I'd rather not get into the exact spot over the phone, honestly. It's the elementary school sidewalk, the street side. If you know the schools, that should be enough to find it.
Well, I can write it up as the sidewalk along the street side of the elementary school, unshoveled since the weekend storm. I'll send it to the crew supervisor. Would you like a callback on it?
Yeah, that'd be fine. It's 401-555-0155.
Let me read that back. 401-555-0155. Is that right?
That's it.

Good. Now, I'll tell you how it generally works. Sidewalks along school property are often handled by a different group than the street plows, so it may be a matter of getting it to the right people. I'll flag it as a safety issue since it's kids walking.

Okay, but that's kind of my question. When will it actually be cleared? Because it's been two days, and the way I see it, the school should have had somebody out there Monday. I'm not asking for a miracle, just a day.
Understood. I'd say you're looking at today or tomorrow once it's with the supervisor. Either way, you'll hear back from us, and if it's not done by tomorrow afternoon, call me and I'll chase it.
Alright. Tomorrow afternoon. I'll hold you to that, politely. [pause] Sorry, my screen froze for a second. Can you say that again, the part about who handles it?

Sure. School sidewalks may go through a separate crew from the road plows. So I'm sending the report to the supervisor, who'll sort out which group goes. And I'm noting that it's near the school and hasn't been cleared since Monday's storm.
Okay. That's reasonable. I just don't get why it sits for two days when the whole street is clear. It's not complicated.
I hear you. With the slush and the freeze after the rain, the sidewalks get hard and they need more than a plow. But that's not an excuse for leaving it. I've got it down.
Fine. Let me just double-check, you have it as the street-side sidewalk at the elementary school, not cleared since Monday, callback to my cell.
Exactly that. Street-side sidewalk, elementary school, not cleared since Monday, callback to the number you gave me. Anything else I can do for you?
No, that's all. Thanks, Lorraine.
You're welcome. Stay warm and watch your step out there.
